topics.topic: Disposition of unconsumed request bodies and connection reuse
questions: When an operation answers or refuses before consuming its whole framed body, must the listener drain the remaining body and reuse the connection, or close the connection without draining it?

When a handler answers without consuming the entire framed body, must the listener drain and discard the remainder before reusing the connection, cancel the stream and close the connection, or keep reading in the background; and which module makes that decision?
When a handler answers without consuming its entire bounded body stream, must the transport drain the remainder, close the connection, or delay/refuse the next request?

quotes:
After an upload's answer, whatever it was — accepted, or refused before any
or after some bytes were read — `owner_interface` discards the unread
remainder of the body without reading it into anything and closes the
connection its listener accepted; a connection that carried an upload is
never reused.
judgement.why: The later surface text decides the observable case in which an upload may be refused before its framed body is consumed: the remainder is discarded and the connection is closed rather than reused.

topics.topic: Handling ambiguous, malformed, or truncated request framing
questions: What happens when a request carries both `Content-Length` and chunked transfer coding, or carries repeated or conflicting `Content-Length` values?

What must the listener do when framing is ambiguous or malformed, including both `Content-Length` and chunked transfer coding, conflicting repeated `Content-Length` fields, an invalid chunk size, or bytes after a malformed terminator?
What must happen when the declared boundary is never reached or the framing is invalid, including premature EOF, malformed chunks, conflicting framing headers or inconsistent duplicate lengths?

quotes:
each request's body handed on as a stream that ends where HTTP's own
framing ends the body — after its `Content-Length` bytes, or at the last
chunk of a chunked body — so that no reader of it waits for bytes the client
sends only after an answer, and no byte of another request is read as the
body's;
judgement.why: Precedence, rejection, and error behavior for malformed or conflicting HTTP framing are encoding and contract questions for State 6, not State 3 module ownership.

topics.topic: Supported HTTP versions and request-body framing modes
questions: Which HTTP versions and request-body framing rules does the listener implement, including whether close-delimited request bodies or transfer codings other than chunked are supported?
Which HTTP versions and body-framing forms do the listeners support, including HTTP/1.0 close-delimited bodies and HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 end-of-stream framing?
Which HTTP versions and request-framing modes must the two listeners accept, and are requests using any other mode refused?

judgement.why: The accepted HTTP versions and their supported body-framing forms are external protocol and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Timeouts and error signaling for stalled or incomplete request bodies
questions: What ends a request whose client stalls, closes early, sends fewer than its declared bytes, or never sends the last chunk, and is there a body-read deadline?

What happens when the client sends fewer than its declared bytes, never sends the terminating chunk, stalls between bytes, or disconnects early; specifically, what timeout applies and does the stream report EOF, a framing error, or cancellation?
How long may the stream wait for the next body byte or the framing terminator, and which module owns cancellation, timeout and resource release for a stalled body?
